subject.title: Add dependency scanning for package releases

question: Should a high-confidence OSV MAL advisory automatically set an existing ClawHub package release to malicious and block its download, and what correction or rescan path is required if that intelligence changes?
rationale: The proposed implementation changes the marketplace trust boundary and can revoke download access based on an external advisory feed; source inspection cannot determine the repository's intended long-term policy for false positives, advisory retractions, or release restoration.

options.title: Approve exact-release blocking
options.body: Accept OSV MAL advisories as the defined high-confidence source, provided the policy records rescan and reversal behavior for changed or withdrawn advisories.

options.title: Keep findings advisory
options.body: Persist and expose dependency findings but require moderation or an additional signal before changing public download eligibility.

options.title: Pause for a broader trust-policy RFC
options.body: Defer this implementation until maintainers define a shared supply-chain intelligence and false-positive policy.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-release blocking
recommendation.body: Accept OSV MAL advisories as the defined high-confidence source, provided the policy records rescan and reversal behavior for changed or withdrawn advisories.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged package-inspector work is the closest evidenced package-security history available in the reviewed context.
